title: ServiceNow vs. Palantir Technologies: Comparing Steady Sales Scale Against Rapid Revenue Acceleration
author: Robert Izquierdo
description: Palantir Technologies is experiencing rapid revenue acceleration, growing Q3 2026 sales 96% year-over-year to $2.3 billion, driven by its commercial AI platform (AIP) which surpassed government revenue for the first time. ServiceNow maintains steady growth at 20.5% year-over-year in Q3 with $4.1 billion in revenue, but faces margin pressure as costs rise. Palantir's net income surged 49% while ServiceNow's declined year-over-year, explaining the significant valuation difference between the two companies.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: ServiceNow demonstrates consistent but modest revenue growth (20.5% YoY) and maintains a larger absolute revenue base ($4.1B). However, profitability declined significantly with Q3 net income falling from $502M to $277M year-over-year due to rising costs, offsetting positive revenue trends.

Palantir shows exceptional revenue acceleration with 96% YoY growth in Q3 2026 to $2.3 billion, driven by successful commercial expansion of its AI platform (AIP). U.S. commercial revenue surpassed government revenue for the first time, and net income surged 49% YoY to $1.1 billion, demonstrating strong profitability alongside rapid growth.

title: eGain lanceert Trusted Knowledge Service om bedrijfskennis AI-klaar te maken zonder bestaande platforms te vervangen
author: Egain Corporation
description: eGain announced the Trusted Knowledge Service, a new expert service that assesses, improves, and validates knowledge quality in existing platforms like SharePoint, Confluence, ServiceNow, and Salesforce to make enterprise knowledge AI-ready without requiring platform replacement. The service includes four modules: Assess, Ready, Prove, and Run, addressing the core issue that poor knowledge quality rather than AI models themselves limits AI ROI.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: ServiceNow is mentioned as one of the supported platforms for eGain's service, indicating compatibility and integration opportunity, but no specific performance metrics or strategic implications are provided.
Salesforce is mentioned as a supported platform for the Trusted Knowledge Service, indicating integration capability, but no specific impact or strategic implications are discussed.

eGain announced a new service offering that addresses a significant market pain point (knowledge quality for AI), recognized as a leader by Gartner in Knowledge Management Systems, and demonstrated strong customer results with COUNTRY Financial achieving 96.2% correct answers and 25% reduction in calls.

title: 2 Stocks That Plunged on Oct. 29 to Buy and Hold Through 2030
author: Daniel Sparks
description: Marvell Technology and ServiceNow both dropped significantly on Oct. 29—Marvell due to its $115 billion acquisition of Lumentum, and ServiceNow due to lower-than-expected contract revenue guidance. Despite the sell-offs, both stocks trade at valuations below their long-term 2030-2031 targets, making them potentially attractive for buy-and-hold investors focused on AI infrastructure and enterprise software.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Despite a 32% decline from Oct. 28, the stock trades at under 6x its 2031 earnings target of $30+ per share. The Lumentum acquisition adds strategic value with $1B+ in annual cost savings and accelerating revenue growth expected to reach $70-90B by fiscal 2031, making current valuations attractive for long-term holders.

The 32% decline was driven by a single quarter's cRPO guidance miss, but management expects subscription revenue growth to reaccelerate to 21.5% in Q4. With a 2030 target of $30B in subscription revenue and a current valuation of 10x projected 2030 free cash flow, the stock appears undervalued for long-term investors.

Lumentum is being acquired by Marvell at a valuation of ~$115B (including debt) in an all-stock deal. While this represents a strategic combination in optical networking for AI data centers, the acquisition eliminates Lumentum as an independent investment.

title: ServiceNow Drops 29% in a Month: Should You Hold or Fold the Stock?
author: Na
description: ServiceNow (NOW) shares dropped 29% in a month, underperforming the tech sector due to slowing cRPO growth guidance (18.5% vs 21%), rising infrastructure costs pressuring profitability, and increased debt from acquisitions. While AI net new ACV surged 65% with strong long-term potential, the company's premium valuation and near-term challenges warrant caution.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Stock fell 29% in a month; cRPO growth guidance declined from 21% to 18.5%; subscription gross margin contracted from 80% to 74%; debt increased from $1.49B to $7.52B; earnings estimates revised downward 2.7-6.1%; trading at premium valuation (P/S 5.50X vs sector 4.93X). Near-term headwinds outweigh long-term AI opportunities.

title: Where Will ServiceNow Stock Be in 2 Years?
author: Rick Orford
description: ServiceNow has expanded its partnership with Google Cloud to integrate Gemini Enterprise for executing business workflows across multiple industries. The company's ability to monetize its growing AI capabilities will be crucial in determining whether the stock delivers meaningful upside over the next two years.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While the expansion of AI capabilities and Google Cloud partnership presents growth opportunities, the article emphasizes uncertainty around monetization and financial payoff. The stock recently experienced a 27% crash, suggesting volatility and investor caution despite potential long-term prospects.
